Convert standardized analytes to milliequivalents per liter

Source: R/units.R
convert_analytes_to_meq.Rd

Converts standardized analytical concentrations to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L) using analyte-specific conversion factors stored in [analyte_tbl].

convert_analytes_to_meq(
  df,
  analyte_col = ".analyte_id",
  value_col = ".analysis_result",
  unit_col = ".analysis_unit",
  value_out_col = ".analysis_result_meq",
  unit_out_col = ".analysis_unit_meq"
)

Arguments

df

Data frame containing analytical results.

analyte_col

Character string identifying the canonical analyte column. Default is `"analyte"`.

value_col

Character string identifying the analytical concentration column. Default is `".analysis_result"`.

unit_col

Character string identifying the reporting unit column. Default is `".analysis_unit"`.

value_out_col

Character string identifying the output meq concentration column. Default is `"analysis_result_meq"`.

unit_out_col

Character string identifying the output meq reporting unit column. Default is `"default_unit_meq"`.

Value

A data frame containing all original columns plus:

analysis_result_meq

Concentration expressed as meq/L.

default_unit_meq

Reporting unit, always `"meq/L"` for supported analytes.

Details

For env_schema objects, analytical concentrations are standardized during schema construction. This function converts those standardized concentrations to meq/L.

The function validates that analytes eligible for milliequivalent conversion are reported in their expected standard unit.

Conversion factors are obtained from [`.get_meq_conversion_factors()`].

The function validates that all convertible analytes are reported in their expected standard unit before conversion.

Only analytes with a defined `meq_factor` in [analyte_tbl] are converted.

Unsupported analytes receive `NA_real_` in the output concentration column.

Workflow

The following workflows are equivalent:


df |>
  convert_analytes_to_meq()

Validation

The function validates:

  • required columns exist;

  • analytes eligible for meq conversion are reported in the expected standard unit;

  • analyte metadata are internally consistent.

Notes

Milliequivalent concentrations are commonly used in hydrogeochemical calculations and visualizations, including:

  • Piper diagrams;

  • Durov diagrams;

  • Stiff diagrams;

  • Schoeller diagrams;

  • charge-balance calculations; and

  • sodium adsorption ratio (SAR) calculations.

See also

[piper_plot()], [durov_plot()], [stiff_plot()], [schoeller_plot()], [charge_balance()]

Examples

gw_data |>
  convert_analytes_to_meq()
#> Error in .validate_required_cols(df, c(analyte_col, value_col, unit_col)): Missing required column(s): .analyte_id, .analysis_result, .analysis_unit

gw_data |>
  convert_analytes_to_meq(
    analyte_col = "analyte",
    value_col = "result_std",
    unit_col = "unit_std"
  )
#> Error in .validate_required_cols(df, c(analyte_col, value_col, unit_col)): Missing required column(s): analyte, result_std, unit_std
